name: Rogue Streetfighter (Rogue/Unchained Rogue Archetype)
body:
Rogues are sneaky and rely on taking their foes unawares or infiltrating places. Sometimes though, especially in the big cities of the world, you need to throw down and fight. That is where the streetfighter shines.

Other Class Options
Streetwise (Ex)

A streetfighter adds 1/2 their class level to Knowledge (local) checks and Diplomacy checks to gather information (minimum +1).

This ability replaces trapfinding for the rogue and unchained rogue.

Ready to Throw Down (Ex)

At 3rd level, a streetfighter gains a +1 bonus to their initiative checks and to their flat-footed AC. Their flat-footed AC with this bonus cannot exceed their base AC. This bonus increases by 1 for every three class levels thereafter.

This ability replaces trapsense for the rogue or danger sense for the unchained rogue.

Take It on the Chin (Ex)

Beginning at 4th level, the multitude of scraps the streetfighter has been in has given them an extraordinary ability to shake off hits.

Once per day as an immediate action, when they take damage, the streetfighter can roll a Fortitude save and reduce the damage taken by the saving throw result. If the damage is nonlethal, the damage is fully ignored, otherwise half of the damage reduced is dealt to the streetfighter as nonlethal damage. The streetfighter must be aware of the attack to use this ability but they can still otherwise activate it while flat-footed. The streetfighter can use this ability one additional time per day every 4 levels after 4th.

This ability replaces uncanny dodge and improved uncanny dodge.

Lathspell Curses
Curse of Anonymity

Bonus Spells: 0th—ghost sound, 1st—disguise self, 2nd—invisibility, 3rd—major image, 4th—greater invisibility

Curse Manifestation: The curse of anonymity renders you forgettable. You take a -2 penalty to Diplomacy and Intimidate checks but gains a +2 bonus on Bluff checks made to feint and to Disguise and Stealth checks.

Curse Abilities

Blend In (Su)

You leverage your inability to be remembered, even in combat. When you roll for initiative you may also roll a Bluff check opposed by each enemy’s Sense Motive. If no enemy succeeds on this Sense Motive check they may not target you with an effect until the second round of combat, either because they did not notice you or believe you are a bystander. This is a mind-affecting effect.

Counterfeit Image (Su)

Your curse can produce multiple images of yourself to protect you from harm. As an immediate action you can expend a spell slot of 2nd level or higher to produce 1d4 mirror images as the spell of the same name plus a number of additional images equal to the level of the spell slot expended. These images last for one minute and if you use this ability again before its duration expires, the previous duration ends.

False Impression (Su)

You can feed your curse magical power to increase its effects. You may expend a spell slot when making a Bluff or Disguise check and gain a circumstance bonus to the roll equal to the level of the spell slot expended.

Greater Trickery (Ex)

You may add three illusion spells from the sorcerer/wizard spell list to your spell list and to your spells known. These new spells must be of a spell level you can cast. This ability may be taken multiple times.

Mirrorshield (Su) (requires 6th level or higher)

You can cause your enemies attacks to strike themselves. As a standard action you make a melee touch attack. If successful you deal 1d6 damage plus 1 damage per class level and the target must make a Will save with a DC of 10 + 1/2 your class level + your Charisma modifier. Failure means you assume a form that seems to be a mirror of your opponent’s features, though not an exact duplicate, for one minute. While this change persists whenever the targeted creature deals damage to you, they also deal that damage to themselves. They may make a Will save at the same DC to avoid this effect to reduce this damage by half. This is both a mind-affecting effect and a polymorph effect. Once a creature has been affected by this ability they are immune to it for 24 hours.

Mirror Walk (Su) (requires 6th level or higher)

You can traverse reflective surfaces. You may step into a surface that shows reflections of small size or larger and emerge from a similar surface within 50 feet per class level as a standard action. As a move action you may touch such a surface and sense all available exits within your range. You may spend a standard action to examine the surrounding area of each surface you can sense as though by a clairaudience/clairvoyance spell.

Mistaken Identity (Ex)

Whenever you are disguised or polymorphed, your normal form and name becomes undetectable by divination spells and effects.

Slip Through Shadows (Su)

You can traverse through darkness faster than most. When within an area of shadowy illumination or darker you gain a +10 foot enhancement bonus to speed and take no penalty to stealth when moving at full speed.

Sudden Revelation (Su)

Your curse can briefly be suppressed to reveal the nature of your curse and strike fear into your enemies. Whenever you successfully deal damage with an attack while your opponent is flat- footed or surprised you deal additional damage equal to your class level and the target must make a Will save with a DC equal to 10 + 1/2 your class level + your Charisma modifier or take 1d4 Wisdom damage. Once a creature has taken Wisdom damage from this ability they are immune to it for 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect.

Walking Curse

True Anonymity (Su)

When the curse of anonymity reaches its height you can become a formless specter if you wish. As a swift action you can assume a shadowy incorporeal form. You gain a fly speed of 100 feet with perfect maneuverability, become incorporeal, and all equipment you carry gains the ghost touch property.

You may suppress or reactivate the ghost touch property of your equipment as a free action. In addition creatures who begin their turn adjacent to you must make a Will save with a DC of 20 plus your Charisma modifier or become frightened for 1d4 rounds. You can maintain this form for as long as you wish and returning to your physical form is a swift action.

Curse of Consumption

Bonus Spells: 0th—touch of fatigue, 1st—chill touch, 2nd—boneshaker, 3rd—vampiric touch, 4th—enervation

Curse Manifestation: The curse of consumption requires you to constantly absorb the life force of other creatures, and in desperate times, your own. At the start of each day you suffer a penalty to attack rolls and skill checks equal to 1/4 your class level until you have dealt damage to another living creature with at least half as many hit dice as yourself. If you kill a creature with at least as many hit dice as you possess you gain temporary hit points equal to your class level for one hour. These temporary hit points do not stack with each other but the duration overlaps.

Curse Abilities
Consume Essence (Su) (requires 6th level or higher)

Your curse feeds on the souls of those you kill. Any creature you have slain is harder to resurrect. When targeted by an effect that would return it to life, a caster level check with a DC of 10 + 1/2 your class level + your Charisma modifier is required or the effect fails.

Eager Hunger (Ex)

You are driven to attack living creatures and feed on their energy. You gain a +2 bonus on initiative checks.

Feed on Knowledge (Su)

Your curse hungers for souls but you have learned to twist this hunger towards the mind. When you deal damage to a living creature with ranks in a Craft, Knowledge, or Profession skills you can choose to expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher as a swift action to choose one of these skills and gain the ability to make rolls with that skill as though you possessed the same number of ranks as your target. This benefit lasts until you rest for 8 hours but you may only benefit from this ability for a single skill at a time, if you use this ability again it replaces the previous instance.

Fueled by Hunger (Su)

Your curse can grant you a replacement for rest when you give in to it. If you killed a living creature with at least as many hit dice as yourself you need only half as much sleep and half as much food for the next week. You still require 8 hours of rest to prepare spells as normal, but this rest need not be sleep, quiet meditation or simple training still qualifies as rest.

Masochistic Desperation (Su)

You can feed your own curse and gain extra benefit if you do at the cost of your health. You may use a standard action and deal damage to yourself with a weapon which deals slashing damage.

When you do you deal 2 damage to yourself per class level and are considered to have damaged another living creature for the purpose of your curse. This damage cannot be healed until you have rested for 8 hours and while this damage persists you deal bonus damage with melee weapon attacks equal to one-quarter your class level.

Sadist’s Edge (Ex)

Your curse is always ready for violence and makes you especially eager as combat begins. Your critical threat range for melee weapon attacks improves by 1 during the first round of combat.

This ability stacks with other sources which improve your threat range but is always applied last, and is therefore not doubled with effects such as the Improved Critical feat.

Sadistic Invigoration (Su) (requires 10th level or higher)

Your curse lashes out into particularly deep wounds.

Wherever you score a critical hit with a weapon attack you also inflict one negative level on your target and regain 1d10 hit points.

Swallow Pain (Su)

Your curse fills you with constant pains of hunger and you can block out other kinds of pain. If you would take an amount of lethal damage that would leave you below 0 hit points you may instead double the amount of damage dealt to you and it becomes non lethal damage. You may benefit from this ability once per day.

Unburden Item (Su)

Your curse changes to take power from magic items. You gain Improved Sunder as a bonus feat, even if you do not meet its prerequisites.

Whenever you successfully sunder a magic item you are considered to have satisfied your curse and you gain temporary hit points equal to the caster level of the item for one hour.

Walking Curse
Gluttonous Soul (Su)

Your curse can no longer be fully sated by your own will. You continuously exude an aura that culls the weak, any creature that begins its turn within 30 feet of you that has -1 or fewer hit points is slain instantly with no save and you gain the benefits of death knell with the following changes; the bonuses and temporary hit points can stack up to three times, and each time this aura slays a creature you regain 2d10 hit points.

Rogue Talents
Agile Fighting (Ex)

Benefit(s): This ability grants the rogue a +1 dodge bonus to their AC, this ability does not stack with the benefit of the Dodge feat. When using Combat Expertise, fighting defensively or using total defense, the dodge bonus granted by this ability increases to +2.

Finally, the rogue takes no penalty to their AC for kneeling, sitting, or being prone. The rogue only benefits from this ability when wearing light or no armor and carrying a light load or less.

Fast Acrobatics (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 1 rank in Acrobatics

Benefit(s): This ability allows the rogue to move at full speed while using Acrobatics to move across narrow or uneven surfaces. Additionally, the rogue only increases the DC of their Acrobatics check by 5 to move at full speed through threatened squares.

Nimble Climber (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 5 ranks in Acrobatics

Benefit(s): With this ability while climbing, the rogue can make an Acrobatics check against the same DC as the Climb check to be able to climb at their normal move speed without incurring a penalty to their Climb check. A failure on the Acrobatics check means they take the penalty.

Nimble Charge (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 5 ranks in Acrobatics

Benefit(s): With this ability the rogue can charge over difficult terrain or through ally’s spaces. The rogue may still need to roll skill checks to traverse those terrains and their speed is still lowered.

Steady Stance (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 3 ranks in Acrobatics

Benefit(s): This ability allows the rogue to not be flat-footed while using Acrobatics to move across narrow or uneven surfaces or while climbing. Additionally, the rogue gains a bonus on Acrobatics and Climb checks equal to 1/2 their class level to avoid falling after taking damage.

Uncanny Feint (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Improved Feint

Benefit(s): A rogue with this ability can feint once per round as a free action.

Unfettered Defense (Ex)

Benefit(s): This ability allows a rogue to add their Intelligence modifier, to a maximum of their class level, to their AC when wearing no armor and not benefiting from an armor bonus to AC. If the rogue is caught flat-footed or is otherwise denied their Dexterity bonus to AC, they lose the benefit of this ability.
